strict.name: social_interaction
strict.description: Initiation and maintenance of social contact; reciprocal social engagement; preference for social over nonsocial novelty; dyadic conspecific interaction. Mouse anchors: three-chamber sociability (Crawley 2004), social interaction test (File & Hyde 1978), reciprocal dyadic encounter, social novelty preference.

strict.name: communication
strict.description: Deficits in verbal and nonverbal social communication; reduced or absent prelinguistic vocalizations; atypical prosody; limited use of communicative gestures; abnormal ultrasonic vocalizations (USV) in pups. Mouse anchors: USV quantification in isolation (Scattoni 2008), interaction-elicited USV (Wohr 2009), gestural communication proxies, pup USV rate and structure.

strict.name: repetitive_restricted
strict.description: <DSM-5-TR text redacted> behaviors; insistence on sameness, inflexible adherence to routines; compulsive habit-like motor acts driven by distress reduction (OCD) or by intrinsic patterning (ASD). Mouse anchors: Sapap3 KO over-grooming (Welch 2007), Slitrk5 KO (Shmelkov 2010), marble burying (Deacon 2006), nestlet shredding, stereotypy scoring.

strict.name: sensory_reactivity
strict.description: Hyper- or hypo-reactivity to sensory stimuli; atypical sensory-seeking or sensory-avoidance behavior DSM-5-TR Criterion B.4. Mouse anchors: acoustic startle, hot-plate latency (thermal sensitivity), von Frey monofilaments (tactile sensitivity), cliff avoidance, open-field light preference. Robertson & Baron-Cohen 2017 sensory decomposition framework. [2026-07-27 criterion-strict: prepulse-inhibition / sensorimotor-gating is an endophenotype proxy, NOT DSM-5 ASD Criterion B.4 behavioral sensory reactivity; it is reported on the mechanism axis, not scored as a face-validity analog here. This domain scores only B.4 behavioral hyper/hyporeactivity and sensory-seeking/avoidance.]

mouse_domain_routing.changed_2026_07_28: Was mode 'natural', which routed mouse terms through primary_domain, a HAND-AUTHORED domain paraphrase predating the criterion-anchored design. Measured that day: of the 80 terms the criterion-grounded classifier admitted for ASD, only 29 sat in a domain any ASD human target could reach, so 51 admitted terms paired zero times, including the entire nociception and thermosensation cluster that answers Criterion B4's own first parenthetical. The old design was therefore filtering the new judgment. Switched to single_bucket so the criterion admission is what decides, matching SCZ, ID and NCD, all of which already route this way.
mouse_domain_routing.known_limitation_2026_07_28: This REMOVES the pre-criterion gate; it does not yet route BY criterion. True unit-to-unit routing, pairing a mouse term carrying criterion_unit B4 with HPO targets resolved from B4, requires stage 1 to emit a criterion identifier per target. Its current output (07_final_resolved_hpo_terms.tsv) carries only a free-text `category` column and no criterion id, so that is a follow-up and not a tonight change.

stage2_candidate_features.taxonomy_provenance_2026_07_28: Repointed to the criterion-grounded taxonomy for ASD, built by build_stage2a_taxonomy.py from that disorder's own run and from no other disorder. The previous file carried ASD's relevance_tier column verbatim for SCZ and NCD, 11485 of 11485 values identical, which made the candidate universe for those disorders ASD's universe.
stage2_candidate_features.spillover_change_2026_07_28: Was true, and ASD was the only disorder with it on; ID, SCZ and NCD are all false. Spillover admits every mouse term the domain gate calls compatible. Under the old `natural` routing that was a real filter. Under the `single_bucket` routing adopted the same day every term is compatible with every target, so spillover admitted the entire universe: ASD stage 2a produced exactly 43 targets times 1,566 terms equals 67,338 pairs, a complete cross product, of which 65,785 (98 percent) entered through the spillover channel alone with no lexical or embedding evidence. Setting this false restores retrieval selectivity and makes all four disorders match.

stage2_rerank._lexical_downweight_rationale: Lexical channel was originally introduced as a guard against LLM/semantic over-reach in ontology mapping (no established protocol for using LLMs in ontology research at design time). When both Resnik IC AND Jaccard channels are absent (structural_missing=True), the redistribution math inflates lexical's effective contribution from its 25%% baseline to ~35.7%% — exactly when lexical's guard role is also least defensible because there is no ontology channel left to validate either signal. Setting factor=0.5 halves lexical's weight in that case (effective ~22%% vs original 25%%), letting embed dominate (~78%%) for cross-jargon semantic matches like Catalepsy↔Catatonia where token overlap is zero but semantic similarity is high. Validated by parity test on ASD: if ASD headline AUROC is stable (most ASD pairs have IC/Jaccard present, factor doesn't fire), the change is defensible to apply across disorders. Test date 2026-05-27.
